subject: Creativity
title: Openness to Experience: The Creativity Personality Trait
description: One-minute skill: Openness to Experience: The Creativity Personality Trait.

hook.text: Of the Big Five personality traits, one predicts creative achievement far better than the rest: Openness.

buildup.text: Openness to Experience includes curiosity, imagination, aesthetic sensitivity, and willingness to try new things.

discovery.text: Studies show Openness correlates with divergent thinking at r = 0.39 — a strong effect in personality research.

twist.text: Openness is partly genetic (heritability ~57%) but can be increased through travel, art exposure, and novelty-seeking.

climax.text: Psychedelic research shows that a single session can increase Openness scores for over a year.

punchline.text: The most creative personality trait is the willingness to be surprised.

quiz.question: Which Big Five personality trait best predicts creative achievement?

details.summary: Openness to experience is the Big Five personality trait most consistently correlated with creativity. details.whyItMatters: Openness to experience explains why some people naturally gravitate toward creative work. Understanding this trait helps both in selecting for creative roles and in developing creative capacity by cultivating openness.
takeaways: Openness to experience is the strongest personality predictor of creativity
It encompasses curiosity, aesthetic sensitivity, and tolerance for ambiguity
Openness can be cultivated through deliberate novel experience seeking

faq.question: Can you increase your openness to experience?
faq.answer: Research suggests modest increases through deliberate practice. Seeking novel experiences, engaging with unfamiliar art, traveling to new places, learning new skills, and practicing mindfulness all correlate with increases in measured openness over time.

faq.question: Are all creative people high in openness?
faq.answer: Most are, but not exclusively. Some creative work rewards conscientiousness and discipline more than openness. Technical creativity in engineering and programming may depend more on systematic thinking. Openness predicts artistic creativity most strongly.
